findings.claim: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the whole safeParse result, so every successful Google token refresh stores {success:true,data:{...}} as credential.key. This happens with credential sync off as well. The next GoogleCalendarService constructor runs googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) at line 75, which throws, so Google Calendar breaks for each user after their first refresh.
findings.evidence: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29 returns refreshTokenResponse, the safeParse wrapper. Before the patch this line used googleCredentialSchema.parse(...). Other callers unwrap .data: zoom VideoApiAdapter.ts:111, salesforce :98, office365 :264. Two seats executed repros. mattpocock's check.js printed 'returned shape keys: [success, data]'. superpowers' repro.cjs printed 'google key written to DB: {success:true,data:{...}}' followed by a ZodError on the next constructor parse. Neither repro ran against the repo-pinned zod 3.21/3.22: mattpocock used 3.25.76 and superpowers used 4.6.7.
findings.reason: Raised by four seats, and two of them executed repros. Red test: run a refresh through GoogleCalendarService, then build a new service from the stored key; it should throw on the pinned code. The fix stores .data, or makes the helper return .data.

findings.claim: prisma is used but never imported. The file type-checks only because packages/prisma/index.ts declares a global var prisma. That global is assigned only when NODE_ENV !== 'production', so in production getClient throws a ReferenceError, this.conn rejects, and every Salesforce operation fails.
findings.evidence: The file's import list has no prisma import (mattpocock: grep -c 'import prisma' returns 0; open-code-review: grep -n prisma finds only line 96). packages/prisma/index.ts:6-9 has the global declaration and :58-60 has the non-production-only assignment. This is reasoned and was not executed.
findings.reason: Raised by four seats, with a source citation. Red test: construct the Salesforce service with NODE_ENV=production and globalThis.prisma unset; it should reject with a ReferenceError.

findings.claim: getClient has several problems. (1) It sends an unconditional refresh-token request every time the service is constructed, whether or not the token has expired. (2) It writes the new token to the database but still builds the jsforce Connection from the stale credentialKey.access_token at about line 104-106. (3) It bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, so it never calls the sync endpoint. (4) In sync mode its response is still parsed with the stripping minimum schema, which drops instance_url and other fields. (5) The !accessTokenParsed.success branch at about line 91-94 is dead code.
findings.evidence: This is reasoned from the code, with line ranges 73-110 across the seats. ponytail adds that jsforce 1.x refreshes on 401 when given clientId, clientSecret and refreshToken, but notes this was not confirmed against the jsforce source.
findings.reason: Raised by four seats. The finding is reasoned and still needs a red test, for example asserting that the Connection receives the refreshed access_token, or that sync mode routes through refreshOAuthTokens. If no red test can be built it becomes unverified and deferred. ponytail's alternative of deleting the block and relying on jsforce depends on the unconfirmed jsforce auto-refresh.

findings.claim: minimumTokenResponseSchema, the sync-mode schema, does not do what its comments say. The computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to '[object Object]' and collide. z.object then strips every other field, leaving only access_token. Every expiry field is lost. As a result, zoom's expiry_date becomes NaN (VideoApiAdapter.ts:116-122) and zoomTokenSchema fails afterwards, and office365 never updates expires_in, so it refreshes on every call.
findings.evidence: Executed. mattpocock's check.js printed {success:true,data:{access_token:'a'}} for an input that also had expiry_date and refresh_token. superpowers' repro printed 'computed keys: "[object Object]" "[object Object]"' and the same stripped data. open-code-review and ponytail ran node one-liners showing the key collapse. The downstream effects are reasoned. Severity was normalised from Important (3 seats); open-code-review rated it Critical for sync mode.
findings.reason: Raised by four seats, with executed repros. Red test: in sync mode, parse {access_token, expires_in}; expires_in should be missing from .data on the pinned code. Suggested smallest fix (ponytail): z.object({access_token: z.string()}).passthrough().

findings.claim: When a response has no refresh_token, the helper inserts the literal string 'refresh_token' in both modes. office365calendar (CalendarService.ts:263-264) spreads the parsed data over the stored credentials, and its schema makes refresh_token optional. When Microsoft omits the token, the real refresh token is overwritten and later refreshes fail with invalid_grant. Zoom in sync mode stores the literal the same way (about line 117-121). Before the patch, a missing key left the stored token intact.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from the code. office365calendar CalendarService.ts:56 makes refresh_token optional. superpowers' repro output shows the parsed data shape.
findings.reason: Raised by three seats. Red test: parse an office365 refresh response with no refresh_token and merge it as line 264 does; the stored refresh_token should become 'refresh_token' on the pinned code.

findings.claim: In sync mode the helper returns a raw fetch Response, but several callers expect an axios, gaxios or SDK shape. In Google (CalendarService.ts:94), res?.data is undefined, so token.access_token throws a TypeError. In HubSpot (CalendarService.ts:177-198), the Response is treated as a HubspotToken, expiryDate becomes NaN, and the Response object itself is persisted as the key. In zohocrm (:217) and zoho-bigin (:96), .data.error throws a TypeError. Credential sync is therefore broken for these integrations.
findings.evidence: Reasoned: the fetch Response type has no .data property, and the original refresh functions returned axios, gaxios or SDK objects. ponytail notes that the refreshFunction: () => any type hides the mismatch. Severity was normalised from Important (3 seats); superpowers rated it Critical. superpowers says Google's catch swallows the TypeError and returns the stale token, while the other seats say it throws. Either way sync refresh fails.
findings.reason: Raised by four seats. Red test: with sync enabled and fetch mocked, call Google's or HubSpot's refresh path; it should throw or persist a non-token key on the pinned code.

findings.claim: The outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication: no shared secret header and no signature, only calcomUserId and appSlug. The parent app therefore cannot tell Cal.com apart from any other caller asking for a user's live OAuth tokens.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from the code. open-code-review notes that the webhook secret already exists and could be sent. mattpocock rated it Minor and conditional on the intent being an authenticated two-way sync. open-code-review and superpowers rated it Important.
findings.reason: Raised by three seats; severity is the majority rating. With no spec, the sync-endpoint contract is undefined, so a test asserting an auth header would encode an assumed protocol rather than prove a bug. The check that would settle it: confirm with the sync-endpoint owner whether caller authentication is required, then add a red test asserting the header is present.

findings.claim: credentialId (credential.id) is passed as the userId argument of refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId). In sync mode the endpoint therefore receives calcomUserId=<credential id> and returns tokens for the wrong user, or for none. It also bypasses the userId truthiness guard.
findings.evidence: The refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 signature, line 53 credentialId = credential.id, and every other caller passes credential.userId. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Raised by four seats. Red test: with sync enabled and fetch mocked, the request body's calcomUserId should equal credential.id rather than credential.userId on the pinned code.

findings.claim: The appSlug sent to the sync endpoint is 'zoomvideo', but the app's slug is 'zoom'. The outbound sync request and the inbound webhook / App table therefore name Zoom differently.
findings.evidence: zoomvideo/_metadata.ts:16 has slug: "zoom". The webhook resolves apps by slug (app-credential.ts:63-65, 87-88). Severity was normalised to Important (mattpocock and open-code-review); superpowers rated it Minor.
findings.reason: Raised by three seats. Red test: with sync enabled and fetch mocked, the request body's appSlug should not equal the app metadata slug on the pinned code.

findings.claim: Behaviour change. A failed parse used to be logged with the Microsoft response, and processing continued. parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws a generic error with no zod detail, the diagnostic console.error was deleted, and the tokenResponse.success && guard can never be false.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from the code: the helper throws when !success.
findings.reason: Raised by three seats. Minor, so no red test is required. Restore the diagnostic and drop the dead guard.

findings.claim: The webhook secret is compared with !==, which is not constant-time.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. mattpocock, open-code-review and superpowers cite lines 24-27; ponytail cites lines 61-62. ponytail notes that an unset secret plus a missing header is already blocked by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED.
findings.reason: Raised by four seats. A hardening fix; use crypto.timingSafeEqual.

findings.claim: The credential-write endpoint does not restrict the HTTP method.
findings.evidence: Reasoned: there is no req.method check.
findings.reason: Raised by three seats. Hardening.

findings.claim: A malformed body (schema.parse), a bad ciphertext or wrong key (symmetricDecrypt), or invalid JSON (JSON.parse at about line 57) throws, so the endpoint returns an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. mattpocock notes that a commit titled 'Change to safe parse' exists, but this endpoint still uses .parse.
findings.reason: Raised by three seats. Minor.

findings.claim: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED evaluates to string | undefined, not a boolean, although its name implies a boolean.
findings.evidence: Reasoned: it is built with && and no !!. It works for truthiness checks.
findings.reason: Raised by three seats. Minor; wrap the value in !!(...).

findings.claim: The webhook looks up appStoreMetadata[app.slug], but appStoreMetadata is keyed by directory name, not slug. google-calendar, office365-calendar, msteams, zoom, lark-calendar and others therefore return 404 'App not found'. getAppFromSlug (packages/app-store/utils.ts:123) already does this lookup correctly.
findings.evidence: apps.metadata.generated.ts:98,109,110,146 have the keys googlecalendar, office365calendar, office365video and zoomvideo, while googlecalendar/_metadata.ts:17 has slug 'google-calendar'. Reasoned and not executed. No seat report contradicts it.
findings.reason: Appendix (2 seats). Under the agreement threshold, so it is not reported and not fixed this loop. It looks high-impact and is a strong candidate for a follow-up check.

findings.claim: The success check response.statusText !== 'OK' is fragile, because statusText can be empty, for example over HTTP/2. response.ok is the reliable check.
findings.evidence: Reasoned.
findings.reason: Appendix (2 seats). Not fixed this loop.

findings.claim: The refresh URL is hard-coded to login.salesforce.com, so sandbox orgs get a 400.
findings.evidence: Reasoned (superpowers finding 3, lines 75-107).
findings.reason: Appendix (1 seat). Not fixed this loop.

findings.claim: The sync-endpoint response is never checked with response.ok, so an error response is handed to callers as if it held tokens.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. The impact is limited for callers that pass the result through parseRefreshTokenResponse, which throws when access_token is missing.

findings.claim: The sync contract is inconsistent. The comment says the endpoint returns only the access token and expiry, but Lark (handleLarkError needs {code:0, data}), Zoom and Webex parse provider-specific response shapes.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. superpowers separately notes that it did not check whether a sync response satisfies the Lark, Webex or MS Teams handlers.

findings.claim: findFirst on userId+appId updates an arbitrary credential when a user has several for the same app. Team credentials are ignored, and invalid: true is never reset on update.
findings.evidence: Reasoned (lines 62-85).
findings.reason: Appendix (1 seat). Not fixed this loop.

findings.claim: There are no tests for the new credential-write webhook or for the shared refresh and parse helpers.

findings.reason: Appendix (1 seat). Not fixed as a finding, although step 5's red tests will add coverage for the main-list fixes.

findings.claim: The helper both throws on failure and returns a safeParse wrapper, which leaves dead .success branches in callers, for example zoomvideo VideoApiAdapter.ts:104-106. It should return .data and the dead checks should be deleted.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. ponytail rated its combined finding Important. That rating rested on the Google key-corruption consequence, which is tracked on the main list (googlecalendar:97). The salesforce and office365 dead branches are also covered by main-list findings. This residual is dead code only.

coverage: Gate: not run (benchmark mode), so no runnable checks anchor this review. No seat ran a build, typecheck, lint or test, and node_modules was absent. The only executed evidence is the zod repros. mattpocock ran check.js against zod 3.25.76 and superpowers ran repro.cjs against zod 4.6.7; neither used the repo-pinned 3.21.4/3.22.2. open-code-review and ponytail ran plain-node one-liners for the computed-key collapse. Spec axis: no spec, and the commits reference no issue; every seat measured the change against intent inferred from commit messages. Standards sources: CONTRIBUTING.md, packages/app-store/CONTRIBUTING.md, and .eslintrc.js / packages/config/eslint-preset.js. There is no AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or .cursor rules file. Files skipped: none of the 40 files was skipped entirely. open-code-review's preview excluded .env.example, but the seat read it from the patch. ponytail gave only a mechanical check to .env.example, turbo.json, the import-path-only add/callback/_getAdd edits and the renamed decode/encodeOAuthState files, and did not confirm jsforce 1.x auto-refresh. superpowers only skimmed .env.example and turbo.json, checked the import-only edits by grep, and reviewed Lark, Webex and MS Teams only for the wrapper call, without verifying that a sync-endpoint response satisfies their handlers. Seat diversity: no other-model-family reviewer took a correctness seat. Rejections: none; no finding is disproved by the seat reports themselves, and no Critical or Important finding was rejected, so no verifier was needed.
